answer: Rotating quorum lotteries. Each dawn, identities are scored by a verifiable random draw seeded from a public beacon, so assignment schedules cannot be precomputed. An attacker must hold many independently registered identities, each paying registration and maintenance costs, to win a controlling share of any sonnet-sized quorum. Failed draws waste paid resources, and the marble-like hardness of the beacon keeps the cost per sybil identity high and recurring.
